Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier this week. We had an internal follow-up: we ran the basic integration tests and are trying to decide between the Starter Plus and Scale tiers. Two things driving the question:

- Feature bundling: we need session-level KV cache and function-calling for some of our assistant flows; not sure which tier includes those or if they can be added as an add-on.
- Downgrade path: if we commit to Scale now and then later decide to step down after the pilot, are there proration or seat-transfer implications? Procurement needs this spelled out before we move to legal.

Attached is a quick feature matrix we sketched (BlueAI_Feature_Matrix_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm recommended plan and any risks if we choose a larger tier up front? Also flag any hidden costs (e.g., long-tail token overage rates, dedicated GPU burst fees).

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood pricing — clarifying plan choices for evaluation

Hi Molly — thanks for the matrix and clear questions. High level answer first, details below:

Recommendation: Start on Starter Plus with a one-quarter pilot and upgrade to Scale for full production if throughput > 10k tokens/s or if you need sustained dedicated pools. Starter Plus supports function-calling and per-session KV caching via our managed cache add-on; Scale bundles those features with higher concurrent request guarantees.

Key notes (short):
- Feature bundling:
  - Function calling: available on Starter Plus (soft limit) and unrestricted on Scale.
  - Session KV cache: available as an add-on to Starter Plus; native with Scale (no add-on).
  - Autoscaling burst to dedicated GPUs: Scale includes predictable burst credits; Starter Plus can burst but subject to queueing and possible fallback to smaller model variants.
- Downgrade & billing:
  - You can downgrade at the next billing cycle with 30 days' notice. Usage is prorated monthly; reserved credits (commits) are not refundable.
  - Seats and seat-transfer: seats are transferable within your org but prorated charges apply for partial months.
- Hidden costs to call out:
  - Long-tail token overage: overage is billed monthly at the published rate; we can cap it with alerts.
  - Dedicated burst fees: if you exceed burst credits on Starter Plus you'll be routed to a compatible variant (lower throughput) rather than charged automatically—charges only if you opt into on-demand dedicated instances.

I'll attach a concise mapping doc and put together two scenarios (pilot -> upgrade, immediate Scale commit) with cost estimates and a pruning of features you can toggle if you need to step down later. Neha, Rachel — please add any contract caveats (SLA, minimum term) or credit options.

Next step: I can share the scenario worksheet and set up a 30-minute alignment call Monday. Which time works for you?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing — clarifying plan choices for evaluation

Quick add: procurement asks about an early downgrade credit if they commit to a 12-month Scale contract and then step down within the first 6 months. Our standard is no retroactive refunds for reserved capacity, but we can offer a one-time transitional credit (up to 20% of monthly reserved value) to be applied to future usage, provided they keep a minimum of Starter Plus for 3 months post-downgrade. Need legal sign-off, but this is the commercial leeway I can offer.

Also, call out: SOC2 evidence and audit logs are part of Scale enterprise pack; Starter Plus includes redacted logs only (retention 30 days). If they need full retention for the pilot, factor that into the addon.

— Neha
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Molly Harris <molly@blueai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing — clarifying plan choices for evaluation

Molly — adding a couple of operational items you should expect if you go Scale then step down:

- Proration examples:
  - Example A (upgrade mid-cycle): if you move from Starter Plus ($6k/mo) to Scale ($18k/mo) on day 10 of a 30-day cycle, you'll be billed prorated difference for the remaining 20 days.
  - Example B (downgrade mid-term): reserved credits are applied forward; if you step down and reserved credits remain unused, we can convert them to service credit for one future quarter (per Neha's note).
- Feature toggles: we can gate the function-calling concurrency and KV retention independently so you can throttle costs without a full downgrade.
- Billing ops: seat transfers require a short form; we'll coordinate with your procurement contact to streamline approvals.

If you want, I can attach the proration spreadsheet with line-level math. Happy to walk through on the call.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BlueAI_Prorate_Examples.xlsx (if requested)
